To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated the possibility to control the photoresponse of a semiconductor heterojunction by changing the thickness of the topological insulating layer.
the photoconductivity of n-type topological HgCdTe films with x < xcr = 0.16 is positive and nonthreshold, while the photoconductivity in films with x > xcr is negative and nonthreshold.

we observed non-equilibrium electron transport in the terahertz frequency range induced by teraherz radiation in the toplogical and trivial phases of mercury cadmium telluride, which was not observed before.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the non-equilibrium electron transport in the topological state of Hg1 − xCdxTe films.
a new type of photoconductivity in Hg1−xcxTe heterostructures that is caused by the non-equilibrium electron transport in a topological heterojucton.
the study of the photoconductivity of n-type HgCdTe heterostructures under the influence of terahertz radiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the non-equilibrium electron transport in the topological state is determined by the 3D potential barrier and the 2D topologically protected surface states, while the electron transport in the trivial state is determined by 3D potential wells.
the non-equilibrium transport induced by the THz field in the topological state is qualitatively different from the trivial phase.
the photoconductivity is a direct consequence of the non-equilibrium electron transport in a topological heterojucton, which is induced by the THz radiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the non-threshold photoconductivity is a manifestation of the non-thermal electron transport induced by the THz electric field in the topological Hg1−x Cd x Te heterostructures.
the photoresponse of the HgCdTe films with x = 0.14 and 0.16 is determined by non-equilibrium transport of electrons from the 2D topologically protected Dirac states.
the photoresponse is determined by the electron transport in the conduction band, which is controlled by the band topology.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the topological phase of the Hg1−x CdxTe material is not only a unique playground for studying the physics of 3D topological Diract states but also a promising material for the development of THz detectors and sources.

terahertz radiation can induce non-equilibrium transport of electrons in both the trivial and topological phases of HgCdTe, which can be used to study the topological phase transition in these heterostructures.
the non-equilibrium transport induced by terhertz radiation in the heterostructure is determined by the interplay between 3D and 2D states, and is independent of the band structure of the material.
